subject: Cross-border SFTP backup purge timeline & transactional-log TTL exception
messages:
From: Andrew Liu <andrew.liu@cloudsync.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara@northbridgehealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: SFTP ingest: purge window & transactional log retention question

Hi Grace / Kimberly,

Quick intro — Andrew from CloudSync Partners (we're standing up the SFTP bridge that will move nightly backups for NorthBridge Health into your ingest pipeline). Two items the customer raised that we need to align on before go-live:

1) Backup purge timeline: NorthBridge's legal wants the backups retained 180 days (they cited regulatory needs). Our standard pipeline purges SFTP-stage backups after 30 days. Can Redwood accept keeping the raw backup blobs for 180 days while we run your ingestion and tokenization? If not, what are the alternatives (escrow, encrypted handoff, or customer-managed S3 copy)?

2) Transactional / event logs (KV + transaction journal): NorthBridge has a forensics requirement and is requesting a 45-day TTL on those logs (we normally keep them 14 days). Is there any chance Redwood can make an exception (read-only retention for forensic access), or provide a secure export path for those logs for 45 days?

Other constraints: the backups will traverse eu-central1 (Ireland) on our side and will be encrypted with our SFTP key. The customer also asked that key custody be configurable (either CloudSync-managed or customer-managed).

We can be flexible on storage location but need a clear timeline and an updated DPA addendum to show to legal. I've attached a quick manifest of expected files and sizes (backup_manifest_sample.csv).

Thanks — if we can't resolve by EOD tomorrow the customer will delay the pilot.

—Andrew
CloudSync Partners
legal@cloudsync.com

Attachment: backup_manifest_sample.csv (csv stub, 2.6MB)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Liu <andrew.liu@cloudsync.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SFTP ingest: purge window & transactional log retention question

Andrew — thanks for the clear ask and the manifest. Looping in Kimberly (security/compliance) and Karthik (infra/ops) to validate feasibility. High level response below; we'll follow up with concrete options and a draft DPA addendum.

- Backup retention: our hosted SFTP/ingest stage is optimized for short-stage retention to limit storage pressure and cost. Standard retention is 30 days. We typically offer two approaches when customers ask for longer keep:
  * Option A — Escrowed encrypted snapshots: Redwood can place a customer-encrypted copy of the raw backup in an escrow bucket for 120 days (customer-managed keys recommended).
  * Option B — Push-to-customer S3: CloudSync pushes a copy to a customer-controlled S3/GCS bucket after ingestion; Redwood only stores indexes/metadata for 30 days.

We normally avoid 180-day raw retention on our side unless there's a commercial add-on (reserved storage). That said, we could make a one-off operational exception up to 120 days if Legal signs a DPA addendum explicitly limiting liability and specifying key custody and access controls. I'll attach a proposed purge timeline worksheet to show delta impacts.

- Transactional logs: this is more sensitive. Karthik: can you confirm whether we can set a read-only retention exception for the transaction journal to 45 days (no hot replicas, only secured cold store) and what the cost/operational risk is?

Action items for now:
  1) Kimberly — please draft the DPA addendum template and the minimal audit controls we require.
  2) Karthik — evaluate technical feasibility and cost for a 45-day transaction log exception and the escrow option up to 120 days.
  3) Andrew — please confirm if CloudSync can do Option B (push-to-customer S3) as a fallback and share legal contact for the DPA execution.

If we can agree to 120 days + 45-day transaction log exception, we can keep the pilot on schedule.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_purge_timeline.xlsx (excel stub)

From: Andrew Liu <andrew.liu@cloudsync.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara@northbridgehealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T02:15:00+00:00
Subject: Re: SFTP ingest: purge window & transactional log retention question

Thanks Grace — appreciate the clear options. Quick answers from our side:

- NorthBridge legal will not accept us holding customer copies long-term; they'd prefer Redwood hold (for convenience) but will accept an escrow approach. They are willing to meet in the middle at 120 days rather than 180 if we can guarantee encrypted escrow and documented access controls.

- Transactional logs: NorthBridge's security officer confirms 45 days is necessary for certain audit windows. If Redwood can provide read-only cold retention for 45 days (with guaranteed deletion record), that should satisfy them.

- CloudSync can do Option B (push-to-customer S3) as a fallback, but setting that up will add 2–3 days to pilot.

Legal contact for DPA addendum: CloudSync legal (legal@cloudsync.com). Please send your DPA draft and we'll route it to NorthBridge counsel.

If you can get an internal nod for 120/45 we will proceed with the pilot tomorrow morning.

—Andrew

On Mon, Nov 28, 2026 at 09:12 AM Andrew Liu <andrew.liu@cloudsync.com> wrote: > (original manifest attached)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Andrew Liu <andrew.liu@cloudsync.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T08:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SFTP ingest: purge window & transactional log retention question

Thanks Andrew — tagging Marissa from Legal/Privacy to prepare the DPA addendum. Operationally: I'm comfortable with a temporary, documented exception to 120 days for raw backups (escrowed encrypted snapshots only) provided:

- The DPA addendum includes: purpose limitation, precise deletion triggers, proof-of-deletion artifact, and an indemnity carveout for any non-compliant subprocessor action.
- Key custody must be explicit. If CloudSync or NorthBridge insists on CloudSync-managed keys, we require KMS integration and an audit plan. Customer-managed keys are preferred.
- Transactional/log TTL exception to 45 days is acceptable as a cold, read-only retention with strict role-based access and an audit trail. Karthik, please confirm the storage class and cost estimate (cold storage vs. hot replicas).

Grace — once Karthik confirms we'll produce the DPA addendum and a short runbook for on-call and audit steps.

Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

> On Fri Nov 28 10:03:00 2026, Grace O'Connor wrote: > > (proposed timeline attached)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Liu <andrew.liu@cloudsync.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SFTP ingest: purge window & transactional log retention question — DPA addendum

Andrew / Grace — legal has reviewed and prepared an initial DPA addendum. High-level callouts:

1) We can approve a 120-day escrowed backup retention on Redwood's side under the following conditions: encrypted-at-rest with customer-managed keys preferred, documented deletion proofs, and logging of all restoration events.
2) Transactional/log TTL exception: 45 days permitted as cold read-only storage with explicit role and time-bound access (no replicas).
3) Cross-border transfer: require SCCs (or equivalent) and an explicit list of subprocessor endpoints (CloudSync to provide).

I've attached the addendum draft (DPA_addendum_cloudsync_v1.docx) and a clean PDF manifest for signatures (signed_addendum_manifest.pdf). Please route both through CloudSync legal and NorthBridge counsel.

Next steps / action items:
- Andrew: confirm whether CloudSync will use customer-managed keys or CloudSync-managed KMS and send the subprocessor endpoint list.
- Karthik: provide an ops note (short paragraph) confirming storage class and deletion proof mechanism we will use for the 45-day logs and 120-day escrow (expected cost delta).
- Grace / Kimberly: once we have those items Legal will finalize and circulate for signatures (DocuSign link to follow).

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: DPA_addendum_cloudsync_v1.docx (docx stub); signed_addendum_manifest.pdf (pdf stub)
